answer: An agent identity is a hardware-bound credential whose registration requires a 500-unit bond locked for 30 epochs, with the device serial hash serving as the unique pigment burned into the registry. An attacker creating N fake identities locks 500N units and forfeits 100 percent of each bond on a proven sybil claim, plus 30 epochs of waiting per credential. Copying a credential fails because the shared bond penalty raises marginal cost per identity, and any dispute routes to independent jurors who check the device ridge and credential bridge against the registry.
